raw_response:
I've farmed these same 6 mu for 45 years, since I was 20. Never went to school, can't read those characters on the fertilizer bags, but I know my land. My wife passed ten years ago, and my boy works in Shijiazhuang, sends a little money now and then. It's just me now. I'm 65, my back isn't what it used to be, so I hire the machines for the heavy work — the combine for wheat, the tractor for plowing. But the walking, the spreading, the pumping — that's still me.

It's almost Cold Dew now, time to plant wheat. I do the same thing every year, why change? I go to the seed shop and buy that improved wheat seed, the one I've been using. Costs me about 35 yuan per mu. Before planting, I spread fertilizer — I buy two big bags of compound fertilizer for the 6 mu. That's not quite one bag per mu, but close enough. Forty jin a bag, I think. The shop man says it's the one with three kinds, I don't know what the numbers mean but he says it's good. Then in March when the wheat turns green, I buy another bag of urea and spread it. If the wheat looks yellow I might get another half bag, but urea got expensive last year so I'll see. I can't spend everything on fertilizer — I need to keep some cash for my blood pressure medicine and for when the pump breaks.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once right after planting to settle the seed, once at jointing in spring, and once when the heads come out if it's dry. The well water isn't free, the electricity meter spins fast. But wheat needs water, so I pay it.

For spraying, I buy one bottle of weed killer from the shop and spray the wheat in early spring. If I see those little green bugs I get the insecticide too, but last year there weren't many, so maybe just herbicide this time.

As soon as the wheat comes off in early June — I hire the combine, 50 yuan a mu, my waist can't handle the sickle anymore — I plant maize. No time to rest, the summer is short. The tractor man comes to rotary till, then I plant. Maize seed is that hybrid kind, about 45 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the holes when planting, about three-quarters of a bag per mu. Then when the maize is knee-high I spread some urea, maybe half a bag per mu. If the summer rains are good I don't irrigate much, but usually I pump once or twice. Last two years were dry, so I did twice.

For maize weeds, I spray herbicide after planting. The worms sometimes come in August, if they do I spray.

All the carrying, spreading, spraying, opening the water channels — that's me. Nobody else in the house. Takes about 12 days for the wheat season and 8 for maize, spread across the year. I move slower than I used to.

I expect the wheat to give me about 380 jin per mu if the spring is decent, and the maize about 400 jin. Not great, not terrible. Same as most years. I don't try to be clever — clever costs money.
